_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. These are spec-shape-triggered PSA gotchas; the next PSA reprint (connectwise-manage, halopsa) will hit several again.

handfixes.summary: The API entity 'Resources' collides with the framework's generic `resources` table; shadow-renamed to `psa_resources` (table + FTS + triggers + upsert + Search)
handfixes.why: Autotask has an entity literally named 'Resources'. The generator emits a typed table `resources` that collides with the framework's generic `resources` store table; 4.22's typed-FTS triggers then crash EVERY sync insert (`resources_fts has no column named name`). The generator shadow-renames colliding Cobra commands but NOT store tables, so the typed Resources table was hand-renamed to `psa_resources` (with its FTS index, triggers, backfill, typed upsert, SearchX, and upgrade test).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should shadow-rename a typed store table that collides with a reserved/generic framework table (filed via printing-press-retro).

handfixes.summary: The composed-apiKey header-blanking bug must stay fixed: client must NOT re-Set UserName/Secret to empty after setting them
handfixes.why: The 4.22 generated client.go emitted unconditional `req.Header.Set("UserName", ""); req.Header.Set("Secret", "")` resets right after setting the sibling apiKey credentials, blanking them -> all live calls 401. The hand-fix removes the reset lines (the buggy pattern now survives only as an explanatory NOTE comment, pinned by autotask_headers_test.go) and sets the real values. NOTE: the literal blanked-Set string intentionally remains inside the explanatory comment, so this entry asserts the FIX (the documenting comment + the real value-Sets) rather than banning a substring that legitimately appears in the comment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press must stop emitting empty-string header resets for composed-apiKey schemes (filed via printing-press-retro).

handfixes.summary: CheckRedirect deletes ALL custom auth headers (ApiIntegrationCode + sibling UserName/Secret) before a cross-host redirect, not just the primary
handfixes.why: Go's default cross-host redirect handling strips only standard auth; the generated CheckRedirect deleted only the PRIMARY custom header, so sibling apiKey headers (UserName/Secret) forwarded verbatim to cross-host redirect targets -> credential leak. The hand-fix adds the extra Header.Del calls for the sibling credentials.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press CheckRedirect should delete every custom auth header for composed-apiKey schemes on cross-host hops.

handfixes.summary: Novel commands renamed/registered to avoid framework-name collisions: generic newStaleCmd (pm_stale.go) dropped, novel `data-gaps` keeps a unique name
handfixes.why: The 4.22 novel-stub emitter re-emits framework-named commands alongside same-name novels (dup-cobra, first-added wins). pm_stale.go (generic data-layer `stale`) collided with the hand-built novel `stale`; pm_stale.go was deleted and its registration dropped (the transcendence spec keeps the novel impl). The novel aggregation was named `data-gaps` (not a framework name like pm_orphans' `orphans`). A reprint must not re-register the generic newStaleCmd (the root.go comment documents the dropped registration) and must keep the unique `data-gaps` name. (The gate cannot assert pm_stale.go's absence directly - it asserts the documenting comment + the data-gaps name/registration instead.)
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press novel-stub emitter must not emit a stub whose name collides with a declared novel/framework command.

handfixes.summary: Hand-written novel aggregations pass math.MaxInt32 to store.List so they are not silently capped at 200 rows
handfixes.why: store.List(rt, 0) silently means LIMIT 200, not unlimited (same unabsorbed press gap as sherweb/pax8). Every hand-written novel that aggregates across the fleet must pass math.MaxInt32 or it truncates at 200 rows and reports wrong PSA rollups.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix store.List limit<=0 semantics in the press (no cap means no cap).

handfixes.summary: POST-query sync seeds the id-walk filter on the FIRST page (`id gte 0`) and coerces array/CSV body params, so page 1 is never sent filterless
handfixes.why: Autotask's query endpoints require a filter: a filterless body answers HTTP 500 "Value cannot be null. Parameter name: filters", so every POST sync resource failed on its first page and synced nothing (issue #257). The press emits syncResourceStaticBody entries only for body fields carrying an OpenAPI `default`, and Autotask's `filter` declares none, so the generated static body is empty and appendIDWalkFilter ran only once a cursor already existed. The seed is the walk's own `id gte 0` condition, NOT an empty array: Autotask matches records against the filter conditions, so `filter: []` returns HTTP 200 with zero rows and turns a loud failure into a silent empty sync. coerceSyncBodyParam also gained the array/string_csv_array cases the generated query commands already had, so a --param override reaches the wire as JSON instead of the literal string "[...]".
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should seed the id-walk filter param on the first page of any POST-query sync whose body declares a required filter array (or emit a static body for required array params with no default), and coerceSyncBodyParam should decode array/string_csv_array the way the generated query commands do (filed via printing-press-retro).

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For autotask the manifest gained: AUTOTASK_BASE_URL. server.json gained: AUTOTASK_API_INTEGRATION_CODE, AUTOTASK_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: AUTOTASK_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.
